The transition from mechanical to electrical amplification represents a shift from continuous-variable systems to discrete-event switching. Mechanical linkages suffer from hysteresis and wear, creating non-Markovian memory effects. In contrast, vacuum tubes introduce shot noise and thermal agitation, yielding white noise statistics. Both systems can be modeled as linear time-invariant filters, but the electrical version allows for feedback loops that correct errors through Shannon's noisy-channel coding theorem. The key failure mode is bandwidth limitation: if the input signal changes faster than the RC time constant of the circuit, the output will lag, causing phase distortion in predictive algorithms.
